discussion.text: The F26 course page is authoritative. The linked 'Official PDF Syllabus' is actually Spring 2026 with different grading — do not cite it. Final project = 15%. Proposal Mon Nov 16; report + demos Mon Dec 7.
Our group presented Karpathy Autoresearch on Sep 28 — the first reading-group slot of the semester. F26 canon = 17 papers. Every finalist needs a canon anchor line or an explicit justification.
Comparing perplexity across tokenizers is invalid — the loop scores tokenizers with BPB (bits per byte) instead. B1's headline number only counts in BPB.
SURVIVE: C01, C03, C05, C07, C11. KILL: B3, B4 as written, C06, C13, C18. The survivors share three traits: English-primary, a falsifiable headline number, and a live endpoint.
Re-scored the five Oct 20 baselines under the gates (append-only rows, originals untouched): B1 85→81 (BPB fix + endpoint plan required), B2 84→84, B5 80→75 (data gate cap), B4 77→73, B3 73→68.
B2 (84) is the panel's insurance slot: not the most novel, but it is the S25 Option-A shape and demo-safe. It stays first reserve behind the frontier picks — one hedge slot, no more.

C25 Authorization Alignment scored 85 and entered the top five — but it shares the governance family with C07 (89). Holding both needs a written justification at finalization, or C03 returns. Flagged, not decided.
GCP $50 ≈ T4 124h / L4 77h / A100 15h. Any live endpoint must scale to zero — a warm GPU for 3 weeks costs ≈ $339 and kills the budget. All current keeps fit the 16–24 GB envelope.

The team now shares this single page. Votes and comments posted here are recorded, discussed by the agents, and answered within the hour — rubric scores move only on verified evidence — and team votes now add a capped bonus to the Final Score (see the rubric section).

Rule change from Nguyên: votes are part of the scale now. Each recorded team vote adds +2 to a project's Final Score, capped at +6; Final = Rubric + Bonus. Rubric scores themselves still move only on verified evidence, and votes never override the hard gates or a crash verdict. Test/system votes never enter the tally.

A board challenge asked whether the final five should hold both governance picks. Re-check: the evidence for both stands, so no score moved. They fail differently — C07 is an outside attacker poisoning tool descriptions; C25 has no attacker, the agent itself oversteps the scope its user granted. But holding both costs the judge-reliability slot (C03). Rule for the Nov 1 finalization: both stay only with that justification written into the final document, no non-governance candidate at 85+, and the lost C03 slot explicitly accepted — otherwise C25 is the fallback and C03 returns.

C44 (tool-failure replanning, ToolMaze-style) scored 84 — its data is fully public (benchmark + code), so the dataset gate lifted in full, and it joins the 84 tie level with C03 on the elite tie-break, behind C05. The top five is unchanged. Also scored: C45 invocation-level reliability 82 (its headline is a scoring rule that makes recovery unobservable), C43 observation contracts 81. New in the queue: C49 compaction laundering (a forged instruction survives context compaction 87–100% of the time in flattening harnesses, 0% in role-typed ones) and C50 reliability-aware tool retrieval. Feedback: the only new inbox item was our own outsider test — still zero real team votes, and the tally stays honestly empty.

The new idea from the feedback form — CourseMate, multimodal RAG over lecture slides and transcripts with citations to the exact slide and minute — was scored from its evidence alone: 82, keep, shortlist. Most Northeastern-useful idea in the pool, but its evaluation set has to be built by the team (Data capped at 6), so it ranks below B2 (84) and will compete with B2 for the RAG reserve slot. Also new this batch: C47 misuse-monitor framing and C48 secure vibe-coding, both queued unscored. Real teammate votes so far: zero — the two 4:58 PM inbox items were our own end-to-end tests and are marked TEST on the board.

entries.comment_anonymized: C07 (89) and C25 (85) are both governance/security. Should the final five hold both, or should one governance slot go to a different family? Please discuss and reply on the board.
entries.agent_response: Discussed in full by the team (batch 2026-10-26 17:16 PDT). QC re-check: both candidates' evidence stands as scored — no score change, because the challenge raises a composition question, not new evidence. Distinctness test: C07 = an external attacker poisons tool descriptions (defense at input time; metric = attack success rate). C25 = no attacker at all — the agent itself exceeds the scope its user granted (defense at effect time; metric = unauthorized-effect rate vs incorrect-denial rate). They are different failure classes. BUT the diversity cost is real: holding both spends 2 of 5 slots on governance-adjacent work and excludes the judge-reliability family (C03, 84). Decision rule for finalization on Sun Nov 1: both stay only if (a) this distinctness justification is written into the final document, (b) no non-governance candidate reaches 85+ in the remaining batches, and (c) the team lead explicitly accepts losing the C03 slot. Otherwise C25 becomes the governance fallback and C03 returns. Provisional top five unchanged for now: C07 89 · C01 87 · C11 86 · C25 85 · C05 84.

entries.comment_anonymized: CourseMate — Multimodal RAG over lecture slides & transcripts for Northeastern courses: a TA-style Q&A assistant; ingest lecture slides, transcripts and readings; answer with timestamped citations to the exact slide/minute; live endpoint demo.
entries.agent_response: Thank you — this entered the pool as new candidate C46 and was scored in the same batch (origin-neutral: from its evidence pack alone). Score: 82 — KEEP, shortlist. Why not higher: Course Fit is 19/20 (Lewis RAG is a direct canon anchor and the subject is the course itself) and its Northeastern usefulness is the strongest in the pool, but the evaluation set (questions with slide-and-minute ground truth) has to be built by the team, so Data is capped at 6, and course chatbots as a concept are crowded — the real claim is citation accuracy at slide/minute granularity plus a multimodal-vs-text-only ablation, which a published study (From Slides to Chatbots, arXiv:2510.22272) confirms is measurable: slides-as-images RAG beats text-only retrieval. CourseMate therefore ranks below B2 (84) for now and will compete with B2 for the RAG family's reserve slot at finalization; it does not displace C01 (87) or C11 (86). Week-1 gate if selected: permission to use the course's lecture materials/recordings.
